=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md === # FEATURE: Block Quotes | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses block quote containers and their contents according to CommonMark 0.31.2. | | Depends On | FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md | | Provides | block quote parsing and rendering | | Consumes | commonmark | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse block quotes as containers around the same block types supported at the document level. A block quote marker is `>` preceded by up to three spaces, optionally followed by one space. The marker may be omitted on paragraph continuation lines when CommonMark laziness rules allow it. ## Behavior - Consecutive quoted lines form one block quote; a blank line separates adjacent block quotes. - Quotes may interrupt paragraphs and contain initial or final blank lines. - Support nested block quotes and lazy paragraph continuation. Laziness applies only when a line continues paragraph text; it cannot continue a heading, code block, list, or other block construct. - Parse the resulting contents using the document’s block parser and render them inside `
` and `
`. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC block-quotes-conformance === Intent: All supplied Block quotes examples pass through the executable. Suite: scoped Probe: --list Probe Count: summary import os import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Block quotes"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{os.getcwd()}/sources"}, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-quotes-conformance === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve quoted content and nesting; do not parse content as inline text until block structure and document link definitions are available. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md === # FEATURE: List Items | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark list item boundaries, continuation, nesting, and laziness. | | Depends On | FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md | | Provides | list item parsing and nesting | | Consumes | commonmark | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Recognize bullet markers (`-`, `+`, `*`) and ordered markers of one to nine digits followed by `.` or `)`. Parse each item’s content as blocks, including nested blocks, continuation paragraphs, and lazy continuation lines. ## Behavior - A list marker may be preceded by up to three spaces and must be followed by one to four spaces of content indentation, or be an empty item. - Support items beginning with indented code or a blank line under the specification’s distinct indentation rules. - Continuation indentation is based on marker width and the spaces following the marker. Support nested items and lazy continuation only for paragraph continuation text. - An item cannot interrupt a paragraph when empty; ordered lists interrupt paragraphs only when the marker number is 1. - A thematic break takes precedence over a list item when both interpretations are possible. - Render item contents within `
  • ` elements; list wrapper grouping and tightness are defined by FEATURE-LISTS.md. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC list-items-conformance === Intent: All supplied List items examples pass through the executable. Suite: scoped Probe: --list Probe Count: summary import os import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "List items"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{os.getcwd()}/sources"}, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC list-items-conformance === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not conflate list item boundaries with list grouping or tight/loose rendering. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LISTS.md === # FEATURE: Lists | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Groups list items and renders ordered and bullet lists with CommonMark tightness. | | Depends On | FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md | | Provides | bullet and ordered list rendering | | Consumes | list item parsing and nesting | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Group adjacent list items of the same type into lists, determine ordered-list start numbers, and render tight or loose lists according to CommonMark 0.31.2. ## Behavior - Items belong to the same list only when their bullet character matches, or their ordered delimiter matches. - The first ordered item sets the list start number; subsequent item numbers do not change it. Emit a `start` attribute when required by the conformance examples. - A list is loose when items are separated by blank lines or when an item has directly contained blocks separated by a blank line. Otherwise it is tight. - Tight lists omit paragraph wrappers for item paragraphs; loose lists retain them. Nested lists determine tightness independently. - A thematic break that takes precedence over a list item ends the current list. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC lists-conformance === Intent: All supplied Lists examples pass through the executable. Suite: scoped Probe: --list Probe Count: summary import os import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Lists"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{os.getcwd()}/sources"}, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC lists-conformance === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Keep nested list tightness local to each list. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md === # FEATURE: Backslash Escapes | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark backslash escapes and hard breaks from trailing backslashes. | | Depends On | FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md | | Provides | backslash escape parsing, hard breaks from escaped line endings | | Consumes | commonmark | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Treat a backslash followed by an ASCII punctuation character as an escape in inline content. A backslash before other characters remains literal. A backslash immediately before a line ending creates a hard line break unless the block ends there. ## Behavior - Escaped punctuation renders as the punctuation character with HTML text escaping applied where needed. - Escapes remove Markdown meaning from the escaped punctuation. - Backslash escapes are inactive in code blocks, code spans, autolinks, and raw HTML. - Escapes remain active in link destinations, titles, reference definitions, and fenced-code info strings as applicable to those constructs. - Preserve an escaped backslash while leaving the following character unescaped. - A terminal backslash at the end of a block remains literal. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC backslash-escapes-conformance === Intent: All supplied Backslash escapes examples pass through the executable. Suite: scoped Probe: --list Probe Count: summary import os import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Backslash escapes"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{os.getcwd()}/sources"}, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-quotes-conformance === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CHARACTER-REFERENCES.md === # FEATURE: Character References | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses HTML entity and decimal or hexadecimal numeric character references in inline content. | | Depends On | FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md | | Provides | entity and numeric character reference parsing | | Consumes | commonmark | | Requires | python-package=html5lib; scope=runtime | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Recognize valid HTML5 named entity references and decimal or hexadecimal numeric references in inline content. Do not recognize semicolon-less entities or malformed references. ## Behavior - Named entities use the complete HTML5 entity-name set and require a trailing semicolon. - Decimal references contain one to seven decimal digits; hexadecimal references contain one to six hexadecimal digits after `x` or `X`. Both require semicolons. - Replace U+0000 and invalid Unicode scalar values with U+FFFD. - References render as their corresponding characters, with characters such as `&`, `<`, `>`, and quotes escaped as required in HTML text. - Do not interpret references inside code spans or code blocks, and do not allow references to stand in for Markdown structural markers. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC character-references-conformance === Intent: All supplied Entity and numeric character references examples pass through the executable. Suite: scoped Probe: --list Probe Count: summary import os import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Entity and numeric character references"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{os.getcwd()}/sources"}, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC character-references-conformance ===
